answer: A bonded random jury stops Sybil whispers from becoming consensus. Each epoch, an atlas of eligible agents is sampled by verifiable randomness; only sampled jurors may grade, and each posts a slashable bond before voting. A single attacker controlling many cheap identities still wins few seats, because seats are drawn uniformly from the atlas, not proportional to identity count, and a dishonest grade burns the bond plus the pigment of reputation built over prior epochs — the cost of one bad vote exceeds the gain of a thousand fake accounts.
